answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can anchor identity in a stake-weighted reputation kernel: every agent starts as an unproven speck in the nebula of newcomers and earns trust only by completing small, verifiable jobs signed into a public ledger. Reputation accrues slowly and decays with inactivity, so a thousand fresh identities buy nothing — each must pay the same slow climb. A quill of signed attestations from established peers gates high-value work, so a sybil swarm's cost grows linearly per fake identity while honest agents compound one history.
